The third reason the health sector interacts particularly with the broader economy in the

1.4] Pacific is that economic growth, and especially revenue collection by government, is not able to

keep pace with fast growing and, in some cases, ageing populations and their health needs. This

reflects the volatile nature of economic growth in the Pacific determined in part by the

vulnerability of that region to natural disasters and global economic downturns. But it also

[Context: vulnerability of that region to natural disasters and global economic downturns. But it also]
reflects policy decisions by government. Vanuatu, for example, does not levy income tax.

Taxation and other revenue is lower in Vanuatu than in many other Pacific Island countries

(IMF, 2011).

In summary, the health sector has a particularly large impact on the overall level
